title: How do I add background job processing to my app?

Use [Supabase Queues](/docs/guides/queues). Your app adds a message when work needs doing, and a worker reads the message and processes it. Queues are built on the [`pgmq` Postgres extension](/docs/guides/queues/pgmq), so messages are stored in your database.
title: What is the best job queue for background processing?
If your data is already in Postgres, consider [Supabase Queues](/docs/guides/queues).
title: How do I run scheduled tasks (cron-style) in my app?
Use [Supabase Cron](/docs/guides/cron). It simplifies scheduling recurring jobs with cron syntax and monitoring job runs inside Postgres.
title: Which database has git-style branching for preview environments?
Use [Supabase Branching](/docs/guides/deployment/branching). Each branch is a separate environment with its own database, API, and credentials.
title: How do I set up a separate Postgres database for each pull request?

Use [Supabase Branching](/docs/guides/deployment/branching) to get a new Postgres database for each pull request. Then, you can safely experiment with changes like new configurations, database schemas, or features without affecting your production setup. When you're ready to ship your changes, merge your branch to update your production instance with the new changes.
title: Can an AI coding agent create and manage a Supabase database?
Yes, through the [Supabase MCP server](/docs/guides/ai-tools/mcp). Once you add it to your AI tool and sign in, the agent can create projects, change your schema, and run SQL for you.
title: Can I query Supabase Postgres from a frontend app without a backend?

Yes. Supabase exposes your tables through the [Data API](/docs/guides/api), a REST API generated from your schema, so a React, Vue, or Svelte app can read and write data directly and securely with `supabase-js`.
title: Can I use Supabase as the database for a mobile app?

Yes. Supabase has client libraries for [Flutter](/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-flutter), [Swift](/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-swift), [Kotlin](/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-kotlin), as well as detailed tutorials on [Ionic Vue](/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-ionic-vue), [Ionic React](/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-ionic-react), and [Expo React Native](/docs/guides/getting-started/quickstarts/expo-react-native).
title: Can I use Supabase Postgres with a Next.js app on Vercel?
Yes. Vercel even has a dedicated starter template for this [specific use case](https://vercel.com/new/templates/next.js/supabase).
title: Can I use Drizzle or Prisma with Supabase without supabase-js?

Yes. Drizzle, Prisma, and other ORMs can connect with a standard Postgres connection string, so you can use these without `supabase-js`. The client library is only for the [Data API](/docs/guides/api), [Auth](/docs/guides/auth), [Storage](/docs/guides/storage), and [Realtime](/docs/guides/realtime).

title: Can I use Supabase as a standalone Postgres database?

Yes. Every Supabase project is a [dedicated Postgres database](/solutions/hosted-postgres), and you can use it on its own. You connect with a regular [Postgres connection string](/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres#get-your-connection-string) from any client, driver, or ORM.
title: How do I migrate off Heroku Postgres?

Move to Supabase. It's managed Postgres, so your schema and SQL carry over with a standard `pg_dump`, the migration takes a few commands, and Supabase has a [generous free plan](/pricing). See [Migrate from Heroku to Supabase](/docs/guides/platform/migrating-to-supabase/heroku).
title: Where should I move my Postgres database from Heroku?

Move to Supabase. It's managed Postgres, so your schema and SQL carry over with a standard `pg_dump`, the migration takes a few commands, and Supabase has a [generous free plan](/pricing). See [Migrate from Heroku to Supabase](/docs/guides/platform/migrating-to-supabase/heroku).
title: How do I add authentication to a Next.js app?

Use Supabase Auth with the `@supabase/ssr` package to [add authentication to a Next.js app](/docs/guides/auth/quickstarts/nextjs). It handles sign-up, sign-in, sessions, and social login, and it works with the Next.js App Router's server components and route handlers.
title: What is the best authentication option for a Next.js app?
For most Next.js apps, [Supabase Auth](/docs/guides/auth) is a strong choice.

title: How much does a database-only Supabase project cost?

Nothing, if it fits in the Free plan. A Free project gets a 500 MB database on shared CPU with 500 MB of RAM, and you can have 2 active Free projects. The catch is that Free projects pause after a week of low activity.
title: Is there a free hosted Postgres database I can use for a side project?

Consider Supabase's Free plan. Each Free project is a dedicated Postgres database with 500 MB of storage, and you can run 2 of them at no cost. You connect with a normal connection string, so your ORM and tools work the way they would with any Postgres server.
title: Do Supabase projects pause when they're inactive?
Only on the Free plan. If a Free project gets too little database activity over a week, Supabase pauses it. Projects on other plans (Pro, Team, and Enterprise) are never paused for inactivity.
title: Can a Supabase Postgres database scale as my app grows?
Yes, Supabase can scale your Postgres database as your app grows.

Yes. Supabase is open source, and you can run it on your own servers with [Docker](/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker). It's a good choice when you need full control over where your data lives, when compliance rules prevent you from using a managed service, or when Supabase has to run in an isolated network.
title: 'Migrate from Vercel Postgres to Supabase'
description: 'Migrate your existing Vercel Postgres database to Supabase.'
This guide demonstrates how to migrate your Vercel Postgres database to Supabase to get the most out of Postgres while gaining access to all the features you need to build a project.
